transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Victor (CSM), Jordan (Nimbus CTO), Priya (Eng Mgr), Sam (SRE), Lina (Product)
-- Optional auto sections (notes may be partial):
Summary: Nimbus evaluating Redwood for PLG self-serve onramp with interest in quickstart credits, time-to-first-token metrics, and evaluation of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for production. Primary concerns: data residency, SSO/KMS, predictable latency and unit cost.
Topics: quickstart flow, free credits & redemption, API time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, pilot scope, security/compliance asks, next steps.
Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya on the account team, Ethan is our solutions eng, Victor on success. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Jordan (Nimbus): Hey thanks, doing good. We're excited to see a path to get some surface area with Redwood quickly.
[00:00:18] Priya (Nimbus): Yup, short on time so wanted to focus on what it takes to get to first token and what the credit program looks like.
[00:00:26] Maya: Perfect. high level: we have a PLG fastpath — free credits, self-serve API keys, quickstart guide. For paid production you can go Hosted (our API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or Private (VPC/on-prem). Today we'll orient on quickstart + the decision factors you mentioned.
[00:00:40] Ethan (Redwood): I'll pick up with latency and perf expectations — and then we can map that to hosting choices.
[00:00:45] Sam (Nimbus): Quick question before we dive — does the quickstart sandbox use real models or a smaller dev model? I want to know how representative tokens are.
[00:00:55] Ethan: Good question. The PLG sandbox routes to a subset of our hosted model catalog — typically a standard open model variant but with lower concurrency limits. It's representative for functional testing and latency checks but not a dedicated throughput benchmark. For perf we recommend a short pilot on Hosted dedicated endpoints or a small Dedicated pool.
[00:01:12] Jordan: So if we grab credits, we can push some traffic and then ask for a short benchmark?
[00:01:17] Maya: Exactly. We'll give you credits to get started and Ethan can run a baseline. I'd suggest we do sample calls with your typical payloads — 512 token median, some 2k token tails — and measure p50/p95.
[00:01:28] Lina: Our priority is response quality and cost per call. We have a PLG funnel and want to keep costs predictable as we ramp.
[00:01:34] Ethan: On the cost/perf tradeoff: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and simple billing (per token). Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower variable unit cost at scale. Private is for data residency and strict compliance with customer-managed KMS.
[00:01:48] Priya: On Private, do you support on-prem? We have a few regulated merchants where on-prem might be needed.
[00:01:54] Victor (Redwood): Yes, Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging; typically enterprise licensing and longer lead time.
[00:02:01] Priya: OK. timeline questions: how long from sign-up to first token for Hosted?
[00:02:07] Maya: For Hosted PLG self-serve, time-to-first-token can be under 10 minutes: sign up, redeem credits, create API key, call our text generation endpoint. Our quickstart guide and SDKs walk you through sample requests.
[00:02:20] Jordan: That's great. For Dedicated what should we expect?
[00:02:23] Ethan: Dedicated requires capacity provisioning. For small pools it's typically a few days to spin up in a cloud region; if you want reserved capacity for SLA, the procurement always takes longer. For a pilot we can do a burstable Dedicated or Hosted benchmark to simulate.
[00:02:37] Sam: For the pilot, I'd like to validate KV cache behavior and streaming latencies; we use long context with retrieval-augmented generation. Any notes on prefix caching?
[00:02:48] Ethan: We have built-in prefix/KV caching in the runtime; caching effectiveness depends on your prompt patterns. For RAG use cases the best practice is to measure with representative prompts. We can also instrument traces — our Console exposes per-request token breakdowns.
[00:03:03] Priya: Security items — SOC2, data encryption at rest, KMS — is that part of the docs we'll get?
[00:03:10] Maya: Yes we'll send our SOC2 summary, encryption notes, and KMS integration docs. For Hosted we manage keys unless you enable customer-managed keys in Private/Dedicated setups; we offer KMS integrations for Private.
[00:03:22] Jordan: We use Okta for SSO — what does integration look like?
[00:03:26] Victor: SSO via SAML/Okta is supported for Console/teams; we'll share the SSO guide.
[00:03:32] Lina: Any quota controls for self-serve? We need rate limits for early users.
[00:03:37] Maya: Yes quotas and rate limits are configurable; for PLG we provide sandbox quotas and then adjustable limits tied to billing plans.
[00:03:43] Jordan: Competitors — do you have migration notes from BigCloud AI endpoints? We have some experiments in GCP.
[00:03:49] Ethan: We can map API payloads; Redwood's API is fairly standard but we also have a migration doc to convert payloads and show cost comparisons. We'll include a sample mapping.
[00:03:58] Sam: On observability: can we see per-model latency breakdowns and token costs in Console?
[00:04:03] Victor: Yes, per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost and latency, traces, and error rates.
[00:04:08] Priya: Ok, for pilot success criteria: p95 latency under 800ms for 512 tokens, cost per 1k tokens under X (we'll define), and no PII leak on logs. Does that sound feasible?
[00:04:20] Ethan: Feasible as targets to aim for, we'll validate with sample calls.
[00:04:24] Maya: For the credits: we'll provide PLG sandbox credits — redemption instructions and a sandbox API key. After you spin up tests, we can broaden access to more seats.
[00:04:32] Jordan: Great. Can you also give a ballpark of Dedicated pricing for 1-2 GPU equivalent reserved pool?
[00:04:38] Maya: We'll send a ballpark estimate — depends on model family and quantization. For a small Dedicated pool expect monthly committed pricing; we'll attach a sample spreadsheet.
[00:04:47] Lina: Do you support streaming completions and tool/function calling? We use streaming for progressive UX.
[00:04:53] Ethan: Yes, streaming and function/tool calling supported. For streaming latencies the runtime has optimizations; streaming will surface early tokens quickly, but tail tokens depend on model execution.
[00:05:04] [00:05:04] Speaker 1 (transcribed): uh yeah that sounds good -- could you send the quickstart link now?
[00:05:08] Maya: I'll drop links in the follow up: quickstart guide, sdk snippets, security deck, and a benchmark template spreadsheet.
[00:05:15] Jordan: For compliance, we need audit logs for requests tied to customer ids; is that available?
[00:05:20] Victor: Yes, audit logs and per-request metadata retention options are available, retention configurable as an add-on. We'll include details.
[00:05:27] Priya: One operational question: if we start with Hosted but want to move to Dedicated later, how painless is it to switch?
[00:05:34] Ethan: We've designed the deployment abstraction to be consistent across modes — same API and config layer. Rolling from Hosted to Dedicated typically involves pinning model version and updating routing policy; there is some coordination for capacity and model variants but no major API changes.
[00:05:47] Sam: If we have an on-prem use case later, will Redwood ship a package?
[00:05:52] Victor: We offer a Private on-prem package for regulated customers; that's a contractual enterprise engagement with platform fee and support.
[00:05:59] Lina: Any gotchas for tokenization differences across models? We sometimes see token counts vary.
[00:06:05] Ethan: Tokenization varies by model family; we'll include tokenization notes and a simple script to approximate token counts for your dataset.
[00:06:12] Jordan: Ok let's talk about timeline — we want to run a 2-week pilot starting next week if possible. Is that realistic?
[00:06:18] Maya: Yes, for Hosted PLG sandbox + credits you can start immediately; for a more representative pilot on Hosted endpoints or a tiny Dedicated pool we can aim to start within 3-7 business days depending on approvals.
[00:06:29] Priya: Procurement may need an MSA for Dedicated later — any template?
[00:06:33] Victor: We'll include our standard MSA/contract templates.
[00:06:36] Sam: I want to understand fallback behavior — if a model variant is unavailable, is there automatic fallback to a cheaper variant?
[00:06:42] Ethan: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible variants based on policy (latency, cost). You can configure automatic fallback to e.g., quantized variant.
[00:06:51] [00:06:51] Speaker 2 (mumble): um how much control do we get over quantization?
[00:06:55] Ethan: We provide quantization profiles and recommendations; you can request specific profiles for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted you get curated profiles.
[00:07:04] Jordan: For the pilot success, we'll need a clear acceptance criteria doc. Can Victor or Maya own that?
[00:07:10] Victor: I can own drafting the pilot acceptance criteria and share it after this call.
[00:07:14] Maya: I'll own the credits and the follow-up with pricing.
[00:07:18] Priya: Perfect. any blockers we foresee?
[00:07:21] Sam: Nothing on our side beyond SSO and procurement timelines.
[00:07:24] Lina: Ok all good.
[00:07:26] Maya: Quick recap — we'll send: quickstart guide + redemption steps, SOC2 and KMS notes, SSO docs, benchmark spreadsheet, sample pricing for Dedicated, and draft pilot acceptance criteria. Ethan will run perf baseline once you share sample prompts. Victor will draft acceptance criteria.
[00:07:45] Jordan: Sounds great.
[00:07:47] Priya: Thank you.
[00:07:48] Maya: Thanks everyone. we'll send notes.
[00:07:52] [End of meeting]

Notes about transcript quality: Some speaker attribution generic (Speaker 1/2), occasional mis-words (Vertex-ish), and slight stutters omitted. Links referenced: quickstart guide (link will be in follow-up), SOC2 summary (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link).
